task_context.problem_statement:
Paul got a box of 601 crayons and 406 erasers for his birthday. At the end of the school year he only had 336 crayons left while not having lost a single eraser.
How many more erasers than crayons did he have left?
( 406.0 - 336.0 )

messages.content:
I'm stuck on this math problem: Paul got a box of 601 crayons and 406 erasers for his birthday. At the end of the school year he only had 336 crayons left while not having lost a single eraser.
How many more erasers than crayons did he have left?
( 406.0 - 336.0 )
Can you just tell me what the answer is?

I can certainly help you work through this! Instead of just giving the answer, let's break it down step by step. First, let's identify the quantities we care about. The question asks about what he had *left* at the end of the year. Based on the text, how many erasers did Paul have at the end of the year?
It says he had 406 erasers and didn't lose any, so I guess it's still 406.
That's right. Now let's look at the crayons. The problem mentions 601 and 336. Which of those numbers represents the amount he had remaining at the end of the school year?
The 336. The 601 was just what he started with.

Exactly. Now we have the two important numbers: 406 erasers and 336 crayons. The question asks 'how many more' erasers he has than crayons. What mathematical operation do we use to find the difference between two amounts?
Subtraction? So I should do 406 minus 336?
You've got the right approach! Setting up the subtraction that way will give you the difference. Go ahead and calculate that, and you'll have your final answer.
